clue.text: Have impossible aims: go after bad weather gives way

parts.note: to go after something is to pursue or chase it
rain is the commonest bad weather
someone who gives way defers, or bows, to another

explanation.surface: Someone with unrealistic goals pursues a storm until it relents.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes pursuing an unattainable goal, as a rainbow can never be reached.

clue.text: Unscrupulous lawyer heading off one's constant suppressed laughter

indicators.note: the lawyer word loses its heading, its first letter

parts.note: a shyster is a dishonest, unscrupulous lawyer

indicators.note: the letters for one's hold down, or suppress, the constant inside them

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
C is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer stifles a giggle as an incessant fit of mirth is held in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed laughter' reads as one phrase, but only 'laughter' defines; 'suppressed' signals one's holding the constant, and 'heading off' drops the lawyer's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fits of uncontrollable laughter are often called hysterics, as in 'the audience was in hysterics'.

clue.text: Said by some to have risen rapidly, but cut

indicators.note: only some speakers, those who drop the R, pronounce the two words identically

parts.note: something that rose rapidly soared

explanation.surface: A rumour that something shot up turns out, instead, to have been a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic (southern British) speech, SOARED and SAWED sound the same; 'by some' admits that rhotic speakers will not hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To saw wood is to cut it, so the past tense means having cut.

clue.text: Stiff sort of card supports equipment

indicators.note: in a down light the card sits below, holding up the equipment word

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as for drilling or sound
an ID card is a sort of card

explanation.surface: A stiff card is used as backing for some kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid and stiff are synonyms for something that will not bend.

clue.text: Succeeded dodging fare-checker? Outcome finally undisclosed

indicators.note: the succeeded letter is avoided, so it drops out of the inspector

parts.note: a ticket inspector checks fares
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word outcome

explanation.surface: A fare-dodger slips past the ticket inspector, and nobody hears how it ended.
explanation.walkthrough: IN PECTORE is Latin for 'in the breast', used of a cardinal appointed by the Pope but kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means kept secret, originally of a papal appointment not yet made public.

clue.text: Innocent bishop deprived of golden fabric?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lamé is a fabric woven with gold or silver thread
the suffix -less means lacking or deprived of

explanation.surface: A blameless cleric has been stripped of his gold vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'bishop deprived of golden fabric' as B + LAME + LESS: a bishop without lamé.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is innocent cannot be faulted, so is free of any blame.

clue.text: Place question

definitions.meaning: a location, as in 'the ... and when'
a question word asking about location

explanation.definitionFit: The word asks about location and can stand as a noun for a location itself.

clue.text: On vacation, no one may use computers!

definitions.meaning: on holiday, removed from daily life
read as a rule: a way away from IT for all, information technology being computers

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as 'a way from IT all': a holiday where everybody keeps clear of IT, meaning computers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a holiday that removes you from the pressures of everyday life.

clue.text: Approaches some seaside towns for football and rugby

parts.note: to approach someone is to contact them
ports are coastal towns with harbours

explanation.surface: A sports promoter canvasses coastal towns to host football and rugby matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and rugby are examples of games in which players physically collide.

clue.text: Regularly awry is pic: why I go for such a preview?

indicators.note: takes every second letter at regular intervals through the words

explanation.surface: Someone asks why their picture is crooked and whether they should go and preview it.
explanation.walkthrough: The acronym stands for 'What You See Is What You Get': an editing screen showing exactly what will print.
explanation.definitionFit: A wysiwyg display is an on-screen preview that matches the final printed output.

clue.text: Put old boy on back — it does nothing to cure him

definitions.text: it does nothing to cure him

parts.note: to put something is to place it

indicators.note: the old boy letters are turned back to front

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil is laid on his back, and the treatment does nothing for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no medical effect, given to a patient, does nothing to cure him.

clue.text: Return homework about the French revolutionary

indicators.note: the whole is turned round, as in a revolution
the homework letters go around the French article

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work around the home
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French radical hands back his homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the French article inside the homework, giving DLEIY; 'revolutionary' then turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment's return is its yield, the profit it produces.

clue.text: Movement of eyes in modest lowering

indicators.note: the eye movement goes inside the modest word

parts.note: decent means modest or respectable
REM is rapid eye movement, in sleep

explanation.surface: Someone modestly lowers their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrement is a reduction or decrease, the act of lowering an amount.

clue.text: European visits prosperous kingdom

indicators.note: the European letter comes to stay inside the prosperous word

parts.note: prosperous means rich

explanation.surface: A European tourist goes to a wealthy realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for empire or realm, as in the Third Reich.

clue.text: After heroin, moralist turns to a drop of the hard stuff

definitions.text: a drop of the hard stuff

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: the letters of moralist change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: After taking heroin, a preacher of morality turns to strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' suggests spirits; here it is ice falling from the sky. 'After' just places H first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is hard ice falling, so a storm of it is literally a fall of the hard stuff.

clue.text: Sort of progression of cortege I'm organising

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: An undertaker arranges the order in which a funeral procession advances.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric progression is a sequence in which each term is multiplied by a fixed ratio.

clue.text: Serious distance to one's final destination

parts.note: grave means serious
a yard is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: A solemn reflection on how far one has to travel to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery is where everyone ends up, so it is one's last stop.

clue.text: Lying about boss, nearly new

indicators.note: the new word goes around the shortened boss

parts.note: recent means new

indicators.note: the boss word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an umbo is the boss, the central knob, of a shield

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies about their new manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager, but it is the knob on a shield, UMBO; 'nearly' trims it to UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means lying down, reclining.

clue.text: Chew gum, having drunk tea

parts.note: mastic is a gum resin from a Mediterranean tree

indicators.note: tea that is drunk is staggered, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone chews gum while sipping tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew food thoroughly.

clue.text: Russian cavalry dropping lettuce in bags

indicators.note: the lettuce letters are let fall from the front

parts.note: Cossacks were famous Russian horsemen
cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Mounted Russian troops drop sacks of lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks are large bags, and the plurals match.

clue.text: Doll has teeth and ears in the wrong places

indicators.note: the letters are set in the wrong order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A doll is made with its teeth and ears misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is a prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2, not a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll is the first name of the Shakespeare character whose surname this is.

clue.text: Around the same thing, live and love

indicators.note: the live word goes around the same-thing word

parts.note: to be is to live, giving are
do is short for ditto, meaning the same thing

explanation.surface: A philosophy of living and loving in the same way around the same things.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply.

clue.text: Pasta cooked as appetisers

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pasta is prepared as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish snack dishes served as appetisers.

clue.text: Smooth old jazzmen

parts.note: to comb hair is to smooth it

explanation.surface: Veteran jazz musicians with slicked-back hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small group of jazz musicians playing together.

clue.text: Positive attitude in small company letters

parts.note: Co is the short form of company; the clue wants that abbreviation's two letters named one by one, joined by a conjunction

explanation.surface: A small firm's correspondence shows an upbeat outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' does not mean post: the short form Co is made of the letters C and O, which read as 'C AND O'.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-do attitude is an eager, confident willingness to take things on.

clue.text: Several overtures made by man to woman

parts.note: Leon is a man's name
ora is the plural of os, an opening or mouth, so several openings or overtures

explanation.surface: A man makes repeated romantic advances to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several overtures' suggests Beethoven's three overtures of that name, but it is the Latin plural of os, a mouth or opening, placed after the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonora is a woman's given name, the heroine of Beethoven's Fidelio among others.

clue.text: Caustic, say, about indefinite number admitted to craft

indicators.note: the number and the turned example are let inside the boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: e.g. means for example, or say

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about how many were allowed on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharply biting, just as caustic ones are.

clue.text: Absurd mother's horrid in these?

indicators.note: something horrid is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A child thinks their mother looks ridiculous and awful in a certain pair of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-length casual shorts, notoriously unflattering on an embarrassing parent.
